verdict: Meridian's research is now honest, but the pending structural move — retire the timing sleeves and run C1 at 78% — rests on 2011–2026 tests that exclude 2008, and the −15% mandate has no live enforcement; close both before switching.

findings.claim: The decision to retire momentum, sector rotation and trend and adopt C1 was never tested on a 2008-type crash: every structure comparison ran 2011–2026.
findings.evidence: §4b, §4c and §5 test 2 use 2011–2026/06; §6: earlier studies 'missed 2008' and C1's unscaled DD is −19% with 2008; §5 Faber (2007–2026, includes 2008) cut max DD to −15.0% vs −48.6% for holding.
findings.recommendation: Before switching, compare the 8-sleeve baseline with C1 over 2008–2026 at a matched −15% drawdown; keep the timing sleeves until then.

findings.claim: The −15% mandate is a backtest property, not a limit: nothing live enforces it. The core is scaled to 0.78 so that one historical path (2008) peaks at −15%.
findings.evidence: §1 stop-losses exist only for pods; §6 each portfolio is scaled so 'its worst 2008–2026/06 drawdown equals the budget'; §7 CORE_EXPOSURE 0.78 'fitted on the same 2008–2026 history'.
findings.recommendation: Add a pre-registered fund-level rule (e.g. cut core exposure at −10%), tested including 2008 — or relabel −15% a design target.

findings.claim: Inference: the pod risk budget has no room — the core alone is sized to use the full −15%, yet pods may take up to 30% of fund risk.
findings.evidence: §1 'alpha pods ≤30% of fund risk'; §6 C1 at 78% invested reaches −15% on its own.
findings.recommendation: Fix the split now: shrink the core pro rata as a pod ramps, so core plus pods still target −15%.

findings.claim: A 12-month shadow cannot validate an edge. General knowledge: t ≈ IR·√years, so one year detects only IR of about 2 or more.
findings.evidence: §1 shadow '≥12 months or ≥30 trades'; §5 each lab report states the minimum detectable IR; the Faber shadow is 'judged 2027-09-30' with no stated criterion.
findings.recommendation: Define shadow success as implementation fidelity (live signals and returns match the model within a set tolerance); funding must rest on the pre-registered test.

findings.claim: Inference: monitoring missed live failures for weeks — the problems were surfaced by a review, not by an alert.
findings.evidence: §3 '45 rejected sell orders since July'; 'AVGO's exit failed 11 sessions in a row'; the reconciler itself raised a false drift.
findings.recommendation: Alert the same day on any rejected or skipped order and on book-vs-broker share mismatches; book positions from fills, not from submissions.

findings.claim: Faber is a drawdown tool, not an alpha pod: it failed its alpha test and trails 60/40 on Sharpe.
findings.recommendation: Re-scope its shadow as a candidate core drawdown overlay (ties to F2); make post-earnings drift the priority alpha plan.

findings.claim: C1 keeps the one sleeve that still carries hindsight: long_term_etf's instruments were chosen on 2026-06-28 and its only strong period is 2022. General knowledge: KMLM launched in late 2020.
findings.evidence: §4a all picks chosen 2026-06-28; §4c long_term_etf −3.2 / +0.7 / +12.8, 'almost all 2022'; §7 it is 19.5% of the fund.
findings.recommendation: Pre-register its live evaluation, or replace it in the core with a rule fixed ex-ante (plain 60/40 or Faber).

findings.claim: The non-inferiority margins sit inside sampling noise. General knowledge: a Sharpe near 1 over 5 years has a standard error of about 0.5, and max drawdown is a single-path figure.
findings.evidence: §5 test 2: Sharpe within 0.05 and max DD within 2 points in each 5-year period.
findings.recommendation: Add bootstrap intervals on paired differences, and call the C1 choice what it is: a judgment on simplicity, not a test result.

findings.claim: Inference: after the switch Meridian is a 78%-invested balanced fund with zero-capital pods and nothing fundable for at least 12 months, run through an 8-sleeve engine built for timing.
findings.evidence: §7 SPY 23.4%, IEF 15.6%, long_term_etf 19.5%, SGOV 41.5%; §1 pods start at zero; §6 about 6.5%/yr at −15%.
findings.recommendation: State Meridian's purpose (pod research platform plus passive core) and simplify core execution to account-level target weights to cut operational risk.

findings.claim: Inference: the no-short guard's stated scenario shouldn't arise on schedule — orders placed at 15:32 CT fill at the next open, before the next session.
findings.evidence: §2 session at 15:32 CT after the close, DAY orders fill at the next open; §3 the guard's rationale cites a Friday buy still unfilled on Monday.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guard, but also block a live session while pending orders remain unreconciled, and alert when a skipped sell repeats.

findings.claim: The −3.9 bps slippage compares next-open fills with the prior close, so overnight gaps dominate it; it is evidence of neither low cost nor gap harm.
findings.evidence: §3 slippage 'against the decision-time close'; §2 fills at the next open.
findings.recommendation: Measure cost against the opening price instead. General knowledge: for SPY, IEF and SGOV the cost is immaterial, so no order-type change is needed.

findings.claim: Expected returns are backward-looking and in-sample: 6.5% at −15% uses 2008–2026, with exposure fitted to the same path. General knowledge: bonds had a falling-rate tailwind until about 2020, and the stock–bond correlation turned positive in 2022.
findings.recommendation: Quote a range rather than a point, and stress-test C1 on a 2022-type rate shock.

decisions.why: A sound target for this fund, but it needs a live enforcement rule (F2).
Honest picks trailed SPY; timing beat holding in only 10–36% of 531 candidates.
Since 2018 it trails SPY on return (+10.4% vs +15.0%), Sharpe (0.52 vs 0.82) and drawdown (−37.7% vs −33.7%).

decisions.decision: Retire momentum, sector rotation and trend at the switch
decisions.why: The evidence excludes 2008, where timing is supposed to pay; test with 2008 first (F1).

decisions.decision: Switch to the C1 core at the ~10/11 review
decisions.why: Not until the 2008 comparison is done; C1's simplicity is right, but its risk calibration is in-sample.
Fitted to one path; pair it with an enforcement rule or a safety margin.

decisions.decision: Pod rules (−5%/−7.5% on alpha P&L, 12 months/30 trades of shadow, ramp, ≤30% of risk)
decisions.why: Right shape, but the risk budget has no room (F3), shadow can't validate an edge (F4), and alpha P&L needs a pre-registered benchmark per pod.
Costless — but re-scope it as a drawdown-overlay candidate and set its judging criterion now.
The fair measure for a mostly bond and T-bill book; worth running now.

missed_risks: Inference: correlated drawdowns across the owner's three bots, all long-biased by their descriptions (§8).
Price-data errors (bad prints, missed adjustments) drive signals and the income tracker; no data checks are described.
Infrastructure: the packet has no evidence on job reliability, outage handling or backups.
Rate and inflation shocks hit IEF, the long_term_etf bond leg and SGOV reinvestment at the same time.
The evaluation windows (2011–2026) are mostly a bull market; results may not transfer to a long bear market.
